One occurrence of an event on a calendar, mirrored from a CalendarFeed. A repeating series gives one CalendarEvent per occurrence.
A calendar published as an iCalendar (.ics) feed, which a System mirrors into CalendarEvent items.

When something starts: an ISO 8601 date-time with its UTC offset, written in the local time of the zone named by theTimeZone (e.g. 2026-10-16T09:00:00-05:00 for America/Chicago), or a date alone (2026-10-16) for an all-day event. Unlike theStartTime, which is a time of day.
When something ends, in the same form as theStartDateTime. Exclusive: an all-day event on 2026-10-16 ends 2026-10-17.
The event's UID in its source calendar (iCalendar UID). Shared by every occurrence of a repeating series.

For an occurrence of a repeating series: the start the series' rule gives it (iCalendar RECURRENCE-ID), which stays fixed when this one occurrence is moved. Together with theICalendarUID it identifies the occurrence. Absent for events that do not repeat.
The CalendarFeed an event was mirrored from (value: the feed's UUID).
Where an event takes place, as written in its calendar: a room, an address, or a meeting link.

The IANA time zone (e.g. America/Chicago, America/Bogota) whose local time something's timestamps are written in. The offset in a timestamp fixes the instant; the zone also gives the daylight-saving rules and the place, which two zones with the same offset do not share. Absent for all-day events.
How an event shows on its calendar's free/busy view.
